title: Vancouver Road Safety Analytics
label: GEOSPATIAL DATA ANALYTICS
summary: An interactive Vancouver road-safety dashboard integrating 2.47M parking tickets with ICBC collision data and geographic quality checks.
overview: An end-to-end geospatial analytics project connecting City of Vancouver parking violations (2020–2025), the municipal road network, and ICBC collision data (2021–2025). The workflow standardizes source records, performs approximate geographic matching, audits data quality, and presents road-level patterns through a published interactive dashboard.

sections.title: Research question
sections.text: How do parking enforcement patterns, changes across years, and approximate collision locations vary across Vancouver roads? The goal is exploratory understanding, not a causal or exposure-adjusted road safety ranking.

sections.title: Data engineering and geographic matching
items: Normalize street and block identifiers across 2,472,917 input parking-ticket records.
Use official road geometry for street-range matching and approximate ICBC collision location assignment.
Audit accepted, excluded, unmatched and ambiguous records before generating analysis-ready tables.

sections.title: Dashboard and interaction
items: Explore parking, collision and comparison analysis layers with multi-year filters.
Inspect highlighted road segments, infraction types and road-level change.
Select a location and radius to examine nearby collision counts, severity and involvement categories.

sections.title: Validation and limits
sections.text: A local end-to-end rebuild passed 37 checks with zero failures, one CDN-related warning and one browser-interactivity check skipped by static QA. Raw ticket and collision counts are not normalized by traffic, parking exposure or enforcement intensity; geographic matches are approximate.

contribution: Built Python data cleaning and geographic matching for the original group parking analysis and implemented its interactive Folium map. The later ICBC integration and v12-series dashboard are subsequent extensions; the project documentation distinguishes the academic team contribution from later development.

title: EEG Signal Classification
label: EEG DATA ANALYSIS
summary: An interactive P300 brain–computer interface case study with historical EEG evidence, GRU exploration and a brain-typing simulation.
overview: A 2023 BR41N.IO experiment exploring whether EEG responses to flashing rows and columns could identify an attended character. The browser experience is a later educational simulation, separate from historical model inference.

sections.title: Interactive case study
sections.text: Explore the brain-typing simulation, four-step P300 explanation, historical EEG visualizations and original hackathon archive in the linked case study.

sections.title: Evaluation limits
sections.text: Saved code confirms GRU implementations. Historical metrics have not been independently reproduced or tied to an exact GRU configuration. No controlled GRU/LSTM speed or accuracy comparison was established.

contribution: Processed EEG recordings, explored GRU-based classifiers, and investigated prediction performance and processing time alongside the team.

title: Mortgage Financial Planner
label: HOUSING & DECISIONS
summary: Explore mortgage qualification, lifestyle-preserving affordability, rent-versus-buy outcomes and financial resilience in one interactive Python application.
overview: Developed from a housing affordability spreadsheet concept into an eight-page decision-support prototype for British Columbia. The planner separates purchase capital, income screening, monthly cash flow and protected savings, then explores how a purchase could change liquidity and long-term net worth.

sections.title: Model and implementation
sections.text: Python calculation modules support a Streamlit interface with shared scenario inputs, Plotly charts and OpenPyXL exports. Canadian mortgage interest is converted from a nominal semiannual rate to an effective monthly rate. The affordability scan searches candidate prices in CAD 1,000 increments up to CAD 2.5 million.

sections.title: Validation and reproducibility
sections.text: The v2.4.2 GitHub Actions run passed all 70 automated tests on Ubuntu and Windows with Python 3.10 and 3.12. These regression checks cover calculation behavior and selected interface structure; they do not establish lending-policy compliance or forecast accuracy.

contribution: Developed the planner through iterative financial modeling, interface design and scenario testing. The project combines Python calculation modules, a shared scenario workflow, interactive visualizations, conditional decision pathways, regression tests and publishing documentation.

title: Crude Oil Pricing Research
label: 2020 IDEA / 2026 EVIDENCE
summary: Follow oil from shipping routes to storage and daily life, then explore price assumptions and the limits of forecasting.
overview: This project revisits an undergraduate question about fear, trading and shipping during the 2020 oil collapse, then builds a narrower empirical test: can a price forecast improve on keeping today's price? The extension includes 2026 market stress, with frozen official EIA and Cboe observations, chronological backtests and explicit distinctions between verified data, assumptions and forecasts.

sections.title: Limitations & next evidence
items: The price response and shipping buffer are assumed scenarios, not measured causal effects or live tank levels.
Small historical model gains remain uncertain. Wider prediction ranges do not guarantee future reliability.
The next test needs new forecasts recorded before their outcomes, using methods fixed in advance.

contribution: Reconstructed and audited the original equations and code; assembled official frozen datasets; implemented chronological model comparisons, robustness checks and prediction-range diagnostics; and translated the results into a four-chapter research dashboard and a shipping-to-daily-life illustration.

title: Hotel Security Decision Support
label: CYBERSECURITY DECISION SUPPORT
summary: Trace five hotel security scenarios, compare original and improved defenses, and prioritize controls within a limited budget.
overview: A browser-local decision-support prototype translates a hotel security architecture case into a multi-floor hotel and synchronized network map. A shared scenario timeline explains entry points, propagation, containment and conditional recovery. A budget optimizer and editable access policy make control trade-offs inspectable.

sections.title: Problem and approach
sections.text: How can a hotel explain incident impact and prioritize security improvements without hiding the assumptions behind a risk score? Five synthetic scenarios connect visible incident paths with selected defenses and budget-constrained control choices.

sections.title: Evidence and limitations
sections.text: The academic report and presentation are available as privacy-redacted PDFs. Layouts, costs, effectiveness and numerical results are illustrative extensions; no live attacks, real customer data or measured security outcomes are claimed.

contribution: The original security plan was a collaborative academic project. The portfolio extension presents a working simulation, transparent assumptions and privacy-safe evidence; individual authorship of every original component is not claimed.

overview: A movie-night research story connecting real observations to controlled comparisons, model diagnostics, and downloadable datasets.
contribution: Personal storage experiment, statistical reproduction and interactive presentation; a separately attributed flavour reference study.

title: Cryptography & Financial Cybersecurity
label: CRYPTOGRAPHY / PAYMENT DEFENSE
summary: Follow a payment through real browser cryptography, compare attack and defense paths, and inspect what reaches the recipient.
overview: A unified portfolio extension built around two group research papers on blockchain risk and post-quantum cryptography. Real browser cryptographic computations are separated from illustrative attacks, account balances and approval policies.

sections.title: Payment defense arena
items: Compare unprotected and defended flows across recipient substitution, signer misuse, replay, eavesdropping and normal payment.
Play, pause or step through signing, transmission, attack, verification and synthetic settlement.
Inspect AES-GCM wire bytes, ECDSA signatures and SHA-256 hash-linked records.

sections.title: Evidence and limits
sections.text: Two privacy-redacted group papers remain available as historical sources. Current explanations correct the original RSA/Riemann hypothesis error and distinguish modern NIST signature standards from executed browser algorithms. All money movements are synthetic.

contribution: Research contributor on two collaborative group papers. This interactive browser lab is a subsequent portfolio extension; it does not assert sole authorship of the papers or a specific original team task allocation.

title: U.S. Treasury Yield Analysis
label: YIELDS & FORECASTS
summary: Analysis of U.S. 10-year Treasury yields across recession periods using ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting in R.
overview: A time-series project analyzing U.S. 10-year Treasury yields across recession periods and using ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting. The project combines statistical modeling in R with economic interpretation and forecast evaluation.

sections.title: Analysis question
sections.text: The project examines how the yield series behaves across recession periods and how time-series models can be used to forecast it. The emphasis is on describing the series, modeling its temporal structure and interpreting forecasts in an economic context.

sections.title: Methods and tools
items: R for the time-series analysis and modeling workflow.
U.S. 10-year Treasury yields as the series under study.
Recession periods as context for examining historical behavior.
ARIMA and SARIMA as forecasting approaches.
Forecast evaluation and economic interpretation as parts of the analysis.

sections.title: Model comparison
sections.text: A dedicated comparison area is reserved for model specifications, evaluation windows and forecast results. No winning model, accuracy improvement or numerical performance claim is made until those results are added and checked.

sections.title: Interpretation and limitations
sections.text: This is an academic analysis of a historical yield series. Forecasts depend on the model specification and evaluation period. The project is not presented as a current interest-rate outlook or financial recommendation.

sections.title: Notebook and reproducibility
sections.text: A notebook can provide a readable record of the data preparation, model specifications, evaluation approach and interpretation. The notebook link and final model-comparison results are still to be added.
